text:
The Blackhawks found out this week that Connor Bedard had shoulder surgery and will be out about four months, and they've answered by winning three straight. ESPN's estimated return is March 23. In the four games since he went down, Ryan Donato has taken his spot beside Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi, Bertuzzi has moved onto the top power play, and Frank Nazar's ice time has jumped to 21:44 a night. Nazar is our Sleeper for a point tonight, at 56%.

Kantserov is the reason the losing streak never came. He has goals in three straight, six in all, including his first NHL hat trick against Vancouver, and 12 points in his last 10. Patrick Kane rides a six-game point streak, though he blocked a shot late in Seattle and The Athletic's Mark Lazerus reported he went for imaging afterward. Chicago is also without Bowen Byram and Wyatt Kaiser, who is serving a three-game suspension for an illegal check.

The Rangers arrive off a 5-1 loss in Buffalo and keep losing bodies. Gabe Perreault is out four to six weeks, Oliver Bjorkstrand is out, and Pavel Dorofeyev practiced in a regular jersey on Thursday; Mike Sullivan said he "wouldn't rule him out," per Mollie Walker of the New York Post. J.T. Miller is one assist from 500 for his career, and Adam Fox has five assists in a four-game point streak.

Our numbers have New York at 3.45 expected goals and Chicago at 2.73. That gap is the season in miniature: the Rangers take 53% of the expected goals at five on five, the Blackhawks 44%. Dylan Garand starts for New York, 2.7 goals better than expected this season, against Spencer Knight, who is right at even after a strong last year. Our playoff odds put the Rangers at 59% and the Blackhawks under 1%, so a fourth straight win would be about pride and young players finding their feet, which is not nothing.
headline: Blackhawks keep winning without Connor Bedard
